prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Select Companion"]
1: ["Meet Your Desktop Companion", "Your pet is active on your screen. Click and drag your pet or check the system tray to manage pet settings.", "Click your pet directly on the desktop to interact or hide it anytime."]
2: ["Preparing Your Pet's Desktop Space", "We are getting your companion ready to jump onto your desktop."]
3: []
4: ["Use a clear, well-lit image (JPG or PNG) with good contrast for best custom pet results."]
5: ["Building Your Desktop Pet", "Rendering custom pet animations. This usually takes about 2 minutes."]
6: ["Your Pet is Live on Your Screen!", "Look at your desktop or system tray icon. Click on your pet at any time to interact or open pet settings."]
7: ["We will send a system notification as soon as your pet is ready on your desktop."]
8: ["Unlocks Companion Starter Perk"]
9: ["Sign In to Sync Your Pets", "Please use your primary login to ensure all your pets and unlocked accessories stay connected."]

verdicts.problem: Mentions gifts, perks, or free extras.
